business_scope.primary_industry_name: Leveraged Buyout Acquisition Syndicate and Special Purpose Co

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1992)
Egypt-United Kingdom Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments
Egypt-United Kingdom Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement
Egypt-United Arab Emirates Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2016 on Combatting Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism as amended; Executive Regulations of Law No. 80 of 2016; Unified Companies Law No. 149 of 2018 as amended, including beneficial-owner disclosure provisions; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT regulations and circulars; instructions of the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation and good standing of each non-Egyptian corporate founder and ultimate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or commercial register in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; documents must be authenticated by the originating registry/authority, then legalized by the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate, and finally authenticated by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Legalization Department)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution / shareholders written consent of each corporate investor approving the establishment of the Egyptian LLC and the appointment of managers and authorised signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary / authorized corporate officer of the non-Egyptian corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (origin country notarization, then Egyptian consular legalization, then Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication; Arabic notarized translation required for submission in Egypt)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner and natural person director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority, notary, bank, or public records holder in the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy in origin jurisdiction; if issued as a public certificate, foreign public documents must be legalized through the Egyptian consulate and Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Arabic notarized translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Applicable corporate name clearance certificate issued by GAFI
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Egyptian administrative document; no consular legalization required for internal use

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against: (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) Egypt's national terrorism finance and terrorist entities designation list; (iii) the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list; (iv) EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists; and (v) Egyptian bank and EMLCU maintained Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs and persons connected to PEPs, with a 12-month post-cessation rule, senior management approval, and source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, all in line with Law No. 80 of 2016 and EMLCU directives.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) electronic one-stop shop / investor services portal, followed by entry in the Egyptian Commercial Registry operated under the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate name must be registered in Arabic script. Latin script may be permitted as a supplementary commercial name or transliteration, but the Arabic name controls legal identity. Foreign names must be transliterated phonetically into Arabic and must not conflict phonetically with any existing registered name or violate public order or religious decency.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Islamic or religious designations requiring prior ministerial authorization
International (where capable of misleading as to origin)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 business days of receiving a GAFI or Commercial Registry rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Legal Affairs Department of GAFI, setting out the corrected name, revised transliteration, and a memorandum addressing the reason for rejection. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may file a cancellation/annulment application with the competent Egyptian administrative court. A reservation may be renewed by filing a new reservation request before expiry; no automatic statutory extension is available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in Egypt is mandatory for LLC establishment. For a private-equity buyout SPV, a pure virtual office is generally disfavored by Egyptian banks and KYC/AML compliance officers and may be rejected as lacking commercial substance. A serviced office with dedicated premises and local mail/receipt handling may be acceptable for correspondence, but the company must maintain an identifiable Egyptian address capable of receiving legal notices, tax correspondence and supervisory authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% to 25% annual probability for a non-licensed investment SPV; the risk increases to 40% to 60% where enhanced due diligence is triggered by bank KYC, tax registration reviews, or suspected lack of commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner register preparation and AML/CFT UBO filing support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee plus prevailing compliance market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical registered office / serviced office arrangement for first 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian serviced office or legal address provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for business address service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for professional KYC support services

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Executive Regulations No. 2310 of 2018.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and Internal Statute (Aqd Al-Taasis wa Al-Nizam Al-Asasi) filed through the GAFI One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is set for the investment SPV track; the subscribed capital stated in the Articles must be fully evidenced by a bank deposit certificate or equivalent escrow confirmation before execution of the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole shareholder/managers incorporate the Company as an Egyptian Limited Liability Company under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, approve the subscribed share capital, and authorize deposit of such capital into an escrowed bank account. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office located at the address stated in the Articles is adopted as the Company’s legal seat, and that all filings with GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Egyptian Tax Authority are approved. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary, with authority to execute agreements, open bank accounts, and bind the Company until countersigned in accordance with the internal mandate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (online investor portal, gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Registered agent submits three proposed Arabic and English company names, evidence of activity scope, shareholder and manager identification, and a source-of-funds declaration. GAFI verifies name uniqueness and the permitted ISIC classification for the special-purpose private equity vehicle.
required_dossiers: Three proposed company names (Arabic and English)
Passport or national ID of each shareholder and manager
Notarized power of attorney for the formation agent
Anti-money-laundering and source-of-funds declaration
Preliminary corporate structure chart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected or a compliance query is issued, the applicant re-files the same day at the GAFI service window with alternative names or submits additional KYC documentation as specified in the objection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Bank Subscriber Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian bank serving as the SPV depository institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary subscription account in the name of the prospective company, deposit the approved share capital, and obtain an official bank certificate confirming the available balance and payer identity. For in-kind contributions, the bank certificate is replaced by a registered valuation report.
required_dossiers: Approved draft Articles of Incorporation
Shareholder passport copies and residence permits
Board resolution or shareholder consent to establish the SPV
Commercial registry name reservation certificate
Bank account application form and KYC package
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC concerns, the applicant rectifies the beneficial-ownership declaration, provides a consolidated corporate structure chart, or selects an alternative reputable bank and resubmits the deposit application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles and GAFI Electronic Submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop and competent Notary Public office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and notarize the Articles and Internal Statute; pay notarial and stamp fees; then submit the full electronic and paper dossier to GAFI through the investor portal or physical One-Stop Shop, including the required supporting documents and bank subscription certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (two original counterparts)
Internal Statute (Nizam Asasi)
Bank subscriber certificate of deposited capital
Valid lease contract for registered office
Passport copies and appointment letters of managers
GAFI pre-qualification receipt and name approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a clarification request, the applicant responds in writing within 15 calendar days, files an amended exhibit, and if necessary re-notarizes the Articles before resubmission at the same service counter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Issuance of the Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon GAFI approval, pay the final incorporation fee and receive the commercial registration certificate. The SPV is simultaneously assigned a commercial registry number and a tax-card eligibility reference.
required_dossiers: Final GAFI-approved Articles of Incorporation
GAFI formal approval letter
Proof of payment of all statutory fees
Bank certificate and notarial invoice
Managers' specimen signatures and identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry rejects the filing, the applicant cures the indicated formal defect, uploads the corrected document to the GAFI portal, and requests expedited administrative review from the GAFI Registration Director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Statutory Books, and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate tax registration and VAT status application with ETA, obtain the tax card, purchase and stamp statutory accounting books, and request a certificate of non-application of social insurance if the SPV has no employees, or register any hired staff with NOSI.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
GAFI incorporation order
Valid office lease and Land Registry extract
Managers' passport copies and appointment resolution
Bank certificate confirming capital deposit
Board resolution authorizing tax filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA objects to the tax-card application, the applicant files an appeal with the ETA Deputy Director for Large Taxpayer Services, submits a revised KYC package, and obtains a confirmation letter from GAFI on the permitted financial activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) – not applicable to non-industrial financial SPV
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – the SPV's permitted activity is governed exclusively by its GAFI commercial registration and related capital market or money-transfer notifications; no industrial operating license is required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure financial holding and buyout vehicle with no manufacturing, processing, or physical emission; no EIA registration required under Law 4 of 1994
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams observed; administrative premises shall maintain compliance with municipal solid-waste handling and office paper recycling standards under Law 4 of 1994 and its Executive Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Clearance required for the registered administrative office; a notarized lease, floor-plan layout, and fire-alarm maintenance contract must be filed with the responsible civil-defense unit before occupational use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; unified e-services portal at www.e-ta.gov.eg (also accessible via www.eta.gov.eg), including income tax, VAT, e-invoicing, and e-submission modules; customs counterpart is the Egyptian Customs Authority (ECA) under the Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign or non-resident entity forming or participating in an Egyptian LLC must procure the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and Tax Card (Al-Karta Al-Darebia) by: (1) filing ETA Form 1 (registration request) with the competent Tax Directorate at the place of the LLC's head office or the non-resident's agent's office; (2) submitting attested and Arabic-translated constitutional documents (MOA/AOA), valid commercial registration certificate, board resolution appointing the tax representative, power of attorney, copy of the legal representative's ID, and evidence of Egyptian source activity or permanent establishment; (3) obtaining VAT registration under the same file if the entity makes taxable supplies above or in expectation of exceeding the EGP 500,000 threshold; (4) receiving the tax card and unique TIN within approximately 30 days for income tax and 30 to 60 days for VAT; (5) mandatory enrollment in the ETA e-Tax, e-invoicing, and e-receipt systems. A foreign PE not having a local entity may register directly with the ETA's Non-Resident Registration Unit and appoint a fiscal agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (not pass-through). The Egyptian LLC is an independent juridical person and a fully taxable resident taxpayer under Law No. 91 of 2005 (Income Tax Law as amended by Law No. 14 of 2023). The LLC is taxed on worldwide income at the entity level; losses do not flow through to shareholders; shareholder distributions are subject to a 10% dividend withholding tax. Small and micro enterprises may elect turnover-based final taxation under Law No. 152 of 2020, while large taxpayers with taxable income exceeding EGP 100 million are subject to a 25% rate, and other corporate taxable income below that threshold generally to 22.5%; a 24% rate applies to certain small business income brackets.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not enact an IRC Section 7701 check-the-box or equivalent single-entity pass-through election. Available statutory elections and regimes relevant to a PE buyout SPV include: (1) election for final presumptive turnover-based tax under Law No. 152 of 2020 for qualifying small and micro enterprises (rates from 0.5% to 1.5% of turnover instead of net-basis CIT); (2) election for the 5% capital gains withholding rate on disposal of shares by non-residents in certain cases rather than net-basis assessment; (3) election by a non-resident with a permanent establishment to file a net-basis Egyptian return instead of being assessed on a deemed 15% profit margin; (4) free-zone entity regime election under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 for a delisted investment entity, subject to prior ETA approval of the free-zone certificate; (5) election to claim foreign tax credit by completing Form 25 rather than taking a deduction for foreign taxes. Egypt applies no domestic hybrid mismatch election and has not adopted full OECD BEPS Action 2 rules into domestic law; treaty residence and beneficial ownership determinations operate under the standard double taxation treaty framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and Executive Regulations (Decree No. 594 of 2016), administered by the ETA VAT Administration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration is triggered when the annual value of taxable supplies (goods and services supplied in Egypt) exceeds EGP 500,000; a separate registration applies to imports as an importer of record irrespective of value; persons making only zero-rated exports are still required to register to claim input VAT recovery; registration application must be submitted within 30 days of exceeding the threshold; the threshold is an economic turnover test applied per entity and per separate place of business, not aggregated for related parties unless the ETA deems the arrangement artificial.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt operates a mandatory e-invoicing regime with centralized fiscal clearance through the ETA. All VAT-registered taxpayers and income-tax-registered legal persons, including LLC buyout SPVs issuing any invoice, debit note, credit note, or receipt, must transmit XML/JSON invoices to the ETA e-invoicing platform in real time via API integration (synchronous or asynchronous messages), cryptographically sign each document with an Egyptian Trust digital certificate, and print a machine-readable QR (Khalid/ECC code) on the visualized invoice. Batch submission via file upload is allowed only for asynchronous flows; the ETA validates the invoice, issues an acceptance receipt with a unique internal ID, and checks correctness against declared VAT codes, tax cards, registration status, and transaction category. E-invoices in foreign currency for an export sale are accepted with the FX amount and the EGP equivalent rate. B2C cash transactions are covered by the e-receipt system enforced since July 2023. Failure to integrate or issuance of a non-cleared document attracts penalties of EGP 20,000 per violating invoice and suspension of the taxpayer's e-services until rectification; the ETA may re-characterize the whole transaction and deny input VAT recovery for undeclared invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to: (1) goods physically exported outside Egypt with ECA customs departure confirmation, provided the exporter holds the export declaration and the goods leave Egypt within the statutory period; (2) export-related services directly performed on Egyptian goods at the request of a foreign exporter; (3) services rendered to non-residents that are effectively performed entirely outside Egypt and consumed abroad, including fund management and financial services supplied by a PE buyout SPV to foreign investors if performed outside Egypt and no Egyptian-source consideration arises; (4) transport services related to international transit and export; (5) supplies of goods and services to official development projects and free-zone qualified operations. Zero-rating is claim-based and requires that the exporter holds the complete evidence trail proving physical movement outside Egypt, the foreign recipient's status, and receipt of the consideration in foreign currency; the input VAT relating to zero-rated exports remains creditable against output VAT or refundable in cash through the ETA refund procedure. Egyptian bank exemption from EGP 100 million? Not applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (approved and stamped by the Egyptian Customs Authority, including EDIFACT/ADF electronic acknowledgment)
Bill of Lading (Ocean), Airway Bill (Air), or CMR (Road) evidencing departure of goods from Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement issued by an Egyptian authorized bank confirming receipt of foreign currency export proceeds into the exporter's Egyptian account
Original export commercial invoice matching the customs declaration value and HS codes
VAT sales invoice and e-invoice acceptance receipt from the ETA e-invoicing platform
Export sales contract or purchase order and, where applicable, the certificate of origin issued by the Egyptian Chamber of Commerce
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA scrutinizes export zero-rating claims through cross-matching of the customs ADF system, the CBE foreign exchange tracking platform, banking remittance certificates, and the e-invoicing registry. A refund claimant bears the onus of proving both physical export and receipt of convertible currency in Egypt; failure to repatriate proceeds within the applicable Central Bank of Egypt deadline (90 days for goods, up to 180 days with extension or for certain service exports) results in disqualification of the zero-rating, reversal of input VAT credits, and assessment of output VAT at the standard 14% rate with late payment interest. Fraudulent or deliberately false export documentation to obtain a refund or reduction is a tax evasion offense: the ETA will claw back the entire refund plus a penalty equal to the evaded tax, impose an additional fine of not less than EGP 20,000 and not exceeding EGP 50,000, and refer the matter to criminal prosecution where imprisonment of one to two years may be imposed under Law No. 67 of 2016 and the unified tax procedures framework of Law No. 194 of 2024; repeated or systematic offenses aggravate penalties to up to 200% of the evaded tax and doubling of fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-floating exchange rate regime with partial current-account convertibility and capital-account restrictions. Current-account transactions, including profit remittances, are generally permissible but remain subject to CBE approval or registration requirements, documentary support, and the availability of foreign currency liquidity in the banking system. Capital-account transactions, such as equity injections, must be registered and routed through licensed Egyptian banks. Profit remittance hurdles include a five-business-day clearing cycle, anti-money-laundering controls, and the ability of the receiving bank to source hard currency; no blanket restriction applies, but practical delays and periodic FX stress events may arise. For private-equity SPVs, the right to repatriate invested capital and returns is recognised under Law 8/1997 (Investment Law), subject to CBE registration and Article 40 guarantee rules, which require that the original remittance be tracked and documented.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must repatriate export proceeds and credit them to an account at a licensed Egyptian bank within 30 days from the date of shipment (or such longer period as CBE permits for specific industries). With effect from the 2016/2017 FX liberalisation and successive CBE circulars, there is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio to EGP; export proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or sold into the interbank market. However, under CBE emergency powers and foreign-currency scarcity episodes, temporary surrender ratios and prioritised conversion orders can be reintroduced. The SPV must maintain a fully compliant export contract, customs invoice, and bank trust receipt to evidence repatriation timelines.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore fintech/e-money institutions (EMIs) are not recognised as licensed banks by the CBE and cannot directly hold client settlement accounts or clear EGP. Cross-border and multi-currency treasury services from non-bank EMI providers are restricted; any use of a global EMI for transitional treasury flows would require a locally licensed correspondent or a registered payment-service provider in Egypt, and would face strict CBE prohibition on non-licensed deposit-taking. Direct EMI integration is only viable for auxiliary payments (e.g., expense reimbursements) provided the SPI's principal transactional and escrow accounts remain with a CBE-licensed commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Yes. CBE anti-money-laundering rules (AML Regulation promulgated under the Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002) mandate face-to-face identification and verification of at least one authorised senior signatory (e.g., director or attorney-in-fact) for corporate account opening. Egyptian banks generally require the physical presence of the ultimate beneficial owners or a formally authorised corporate representative at the branch; remote videoconference opening is not a universally accepted alternative and is available only under limited bank-specific discretion. For the SPV, prior to account opening, the bank will require completed customer due diligence forms, board resolutions, and identification of all natural-person beneficial owners holding 10% or more of the SPV. A physical onboarding meeting in Cairo is therefore the default compliance route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex offshore ownership structure: tiers of holding companies in multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chart from ultimate beneficial owner to SPV, notarised and apostilled incorporation certificates of each entity, consolidated beneficial-ownership declaration, an organisational chart showing percentages, and legal documentation for each holding entity. Additionally provide audited financial statements or capital call schedules that evidence commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private-equity SPV with no active operational income
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed investment mandate, SPV business plan, executed share-purchase agreement or term sheet, capital-call and subscription documents, and a source-of-wealth letter per beneficial owner. The bank will require evidence that the transaction is genuine, the SPV has substance in Egypt (registered address, board meetings, accounting records), and no round-tripping or layering pattern exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparties or jurisdictions in the transaction chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD/FAFT-compliant anti-money-laundering correspondence, sanctions screening results for all transacting parties, transaction flowcharts with purpose codes, and legal opinion on the economic substance of all counterparties. The SPV must also supply calendarised identification of ultimate beneficial owners to detect politically exposed persons (PEPs) and confirm none exercises control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually large or imminent wire transfers relative to declared capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An executed capital call notice, signed loan or equity commitment agreement, valuation report of target company, notarised board resolutions approving the wire, and an incumbency certificate. The bank may require the Amwal (Egyptian FATF) and Ministry of Investment registration certificates showing the SPV's licence exemption and foreign-investment tracking codes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from foreign investors must be routed through a CBE-licensed bank in Egypt using the foreign-currency receipt code for direct investment (Code '500' or the CBE's designated purpose code for capital injections under the Unified Registration System). The remitting bank will transmit a SWIFT MT103 with a detailed purpose code and supporting documentation: a copy of the investment registration certificate under the Egyptian General Authority for Investment (GAFI), legal invoices or contribution notices, and a board resolution authorising the wire. The receiving bank will verify the commercial reality of the transfer, assign a special foreign-currency investment registration number, and credit the SPV's multilateral settlement account. Dividends, profit share, and exit proceeds are subsequently repatriable only upon presenting a completed internal revenue repatriation form, audited financial statements, and proof of tax settlement to the CBE-appointed authorised bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements from the SPV to non-resident suppliers or target companies are executed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 messages through the participant's Egyptian bank. Settlement for goods and services under confirmed purchase agreements requires compliant classification of the outflow under Egyptian trade regulations, including: a valid import-export number, customs invoices, an executed proforma invoice, and the designated Harmonized System/EEPC export codes. For syndicated loan wires or acquisition payments, the SPV may use an MT103 with mirroring TELEX through the instructing bank and the beneficiary bank's test-key validation. Where the underlying transaction is structured as a commercial letter of credit (LC), the issuing Egyptian bank will open an irrevocable at-sight or usance LC (form UCP600), with the SWIFT MT700 message sent to the beneficiary bank and settlement completed via MT103/MT202 upon presentation of compliant documents. All disbursements above USD 10,000 are subject to CBE AML screening and electronic reporting to the Egyptian Unified Anti-Money-Laundering System.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore EGP/USD forward contracts with CBE-licensed banks (with two-way pricing, commonly used for balance-sheet hedging of repatriation exposure).
FX swaps between EGP and major hard currencies (USD, EUR, GBP) with authorised dealers, subject to CBE risk-mitigation and margin/collateral requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore by licensed foreign dealer banks, permissible as economic hedges for SPV exposures to EGP volatility where the settlement is in USD; such NDFs are not offered onshore but do not violate Egyptian law for the SPV when booked through an international group treasury centre.

Currency options and simple cross-currency swaps with Egyptian banks or foreign banks duly licensed in Egypt, provided the SPV can evidence an underlying exposure and obtains CBE conformity for the derivative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 19) for LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Corporate Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end; for calendar-year SPV, due on or before 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delay fine of 2% per month or fraction thereof on the assessed tax unpaid; fixed non-filing fine of EGP 500–2,000; intentional evasion penalties up to 200% of the tax for willful misdeclaration; risk of administrative enforcement against bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements (IAF/FS package attached to Form 19)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) via e-filing portal; audited copy retained in statutory books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with Form 19 within 4 months of fiscal year-end; audit report date must precede filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rejection of tax return as incomplete; treated as non-filing attracting 2% monthly delay fine and EGP 500–2,000 fixed fine; statutory auditor's license exposed to GAAP supervision penalty if misstated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Card Renewal (Certificate of Registration Update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority – Commercial Tax Office of jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During January of each calendar year for calendar-year registrants; renewal within 30-day grace window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of tax card privileges and blocked government/notary dealings; administrative fine for late presentation; possible request to rebuild tax file with EGP 500 minimum penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each January for annual renewal of the LLC's commercial registration record; from month of anniversary upon first issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 1,000–10,000 under Law 34/1976; continued default triggers administratively initiated strike-off from the commercial register and loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation (Beneficial Ownership Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation filed together with the audited financial statements (by 30 April for calendar-year SPV); interim updates required within 30 days of any shareholding change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under AML Law 80/2002 (as amended): EGP 100,000–1,000,000 for failure to accurately register/report UBO data; criminal liability for deliberately false statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll & Withholding Tax Settlement (Form 6 Reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority – Withholding Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the end of February following the calendar tax year (monthly Forms 41 remain due by 15th of succeeding month)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly penalty of 2% (capped at 100% of the payable amount) on unsettled payroll and WHT; additional per-return fines for failure to deliver returns; imprisonment exposure for wilful deduction and non-remittance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit under Companies Law 201/2020 where any member holding 10%+ capital demands an audit, where gross annual revenue exceeds EGP 5,000,000, or where gross assets exceed EGP 10,000,000; this PE Buyout SPV (ISIC 6499) crosses the asset threshold due to syndicated loan investments and therefore requires a certified external auditor each fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), converged with IFRS and mandated under Law 201/2020; fully IFRS as issued is permitted for private equity SPVs upon first-time adoption; statutory records must be kept in Arabic with double-entry bookkeeping.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egyptian AML Law 80/2002 requires the LLC to identify and keep an up-to-date register of ultimate beneficial owners; any transfer of shares or change in direct/indirect ownership of 25% or more must be reported to GAFI's UBO e-platform within 30 days; an annual no-change confirmation must be submitted with the annual financial statements and re-affirmed at each commercial registry renewal.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,200 per year for a GAFI-compliant registered office, commercial agency, and corporate secretarial package in Cairo or a free-zone jurisdiction
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 5,000 for a Big-4 audit of a single-asset PE SPV; USD 1,500 - 3,000 for a licensed local audit firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for ordinary LLC buyout SPVs; potential reduced rates are limited to recognized apex status under sector-specific investment promotion decrees (e.g., Suez Canal Economic Zone) and free-zone services subject to prior approval; tax credits and deductions are generally unavailable to pure holding vehicles without actual industrial operating activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 33 (إقرار الضريبة على دخل الشركات) filed via the Egyptian Tax Authority’s electronic portal / www.incometax.gov.eg (ETA e-services portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months from the end of the company’s fiscal year; for a standard 31 December year-end, the filing and full payment deadline is 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer Identification Number (Tax ID) and statutory file number of the Egyptian LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian TIN and the foreign parent’s tax ID in the related party identification schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year end and accounting period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, attach the parent’s fiscal year certificate in conformity with the DTA claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: interest, dividends, fees, and any capital gains directly or indirectly derived from Egypt-source participation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egypt-source income; exclude foreign passive income if treaty allocation applies, but attach the allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party service fees paid to non-residents, management fees, and intra-group interest paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all cross-border controlled transactions and confirm the arm’s length treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions including operating expenses and non-resident WHT amounts, subject to documentary evidence and anti-abuse limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident deductions require dual invoices and upstream withholding tax certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward (maximum 5 years), supported by final prior-year assessments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is available only if the Egyptian filing statements show continuous same-business continuity and no 50% change in ownership without tax authority consent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss offset and arm’s length adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident allocable Egypt-source income must be separately stated in the schedule for treaty rate computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: 22.5% headline CIT plus any adjusted capital base surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Set out the exact tax due, relate it to each source, and attach the relevant treaty relief clause.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments and withholding tax credits per foreign share of profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any withholding payment certificates issued by the Egyptian borrower with respect to intercompany debt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable / receivable after credits and payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident claim requires bank settlement proof and TRC as required under the DTA protocol.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penalty of EGP 2,000 per month or part thereof, capped at EGP 20,000, plus monthly late-payment surcharge on unpaid tax (2% per month up to a maximum of 30% of the tax due); additional discretionary fines of up to EGP 50,000 may be imposed by the ETA for incomplete or obviously fabricated declarations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder should submit a formal DTA relief application to the Egyptian Tax Authority, attaching a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction, an ownership chain diagram, a declaration of beneficial ownership, and audited financial proofs; the payer must retain the reduced treaty withholding rate only after ETA pre-approval or a judicial writ, otherwise the statutory 10% is withheld at source. The DTA relief must be invoked before repatriation and cannot be reclaimed through ordinary refund unless the treaty technical explanation allows for a post-payment credit claim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 20%, interest 20%, and management/service contract payments 20%. Under Egypt’s active DTAs, royalty rates are commonly reduced to 5–12% for industrial or copyrighted royalties, while interest withholding generally falls to 5–10% depending on banking, bond, and permanent-establishment conditions; no withholding relief applies unless the TRC and beneficial ownership certificate are in place before the payment date.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8,000,000 aggregate value of related-party transactions for the taxpayer (Local File); Master File mandatory when the multinational group’s consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 200,000,000 and the local related-party transactions exceed the EGP 8,000,000 threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to GCC states; however the ETA applies a general anti-avoidance doctrine and requires a performing entity with local effective management, personnel, board decisions, financial books, and commercial reasons. A passive leveraged buyout SPV lacking substance in Egypt remains exposed to judicial recharacterization, denial of interest deductions, and deemed dividend treatment under Article 94 of the Income Tax Law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of Egypt-source gains, overstating deductible intercompany interest, fabricating invoices, suppressing bank receipts, or submitting a fraudulent Form No. 33 declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to EGP 200,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 5 years; administrative additional tax up to 30% of the under-assessed tax; mandatory withdrawal of investment incentives and tax clearance denial.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who sign or procure a false declaration can be personally and jointly liable for the unpaid tax; the criminal court may issue a travel ban, freeze director bank accounts, and order asset confiscation; imprisonment is expressly authorized for intentional tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Egyptian LLC functioning as a nominee/letter-box: no local office, no independent board minutes, no bank activity in Egypt, all buyout decisions taken by the foreign fund, and no ordinary course of trade or actual debt rollup.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may disallow the SPV’s existence for tax purposes, impute a deemed distribution to the non-resident shareholder, recharacterize the acquired target financing as an equity dividend, and apply a 10% dividend WHT; under the AML/CFT framework, the entity is also reported as a suspicious shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A nominee director can be separately fined up to EGP 300,000 and disqualified from serving as manager in Egypt; civil liability is asserted for induced tax losses, coupled with a travel ban until full restitution is secured.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare contemporaneous TP files, absence of arm’s length benchmark studies for related-party loan interest, non-reporting of cross-border related transactions, and failure to disclose intercompany funding structures on the Form No. 33 schedules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalty of EGP 50,000 for each unfiled TP Local File/Master File, plus upward adjustment of taxable profits by the ETA with a secondary 8% annual interest on the additional tax found due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Liability is typically fiscal (entity level), but current Egyptian enforcement practice sanctions the responsible finance director with personal fines and, for cross-border fraud, the public prosecutor can expand investigation; international DTA exchange of information proceedings can also expose director bank records and assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a profit distribution, unaccounted return of capital, or implied benefit to the foreign parent without assessing the 10% dividend withholding tax, and failing to report the withheld amount electronically to the ETA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Full withholding tax liability, penalty equal to 30% of the unreported withholding amount, and criminal fine up to EGP 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible managing director is jointly liable as withholding agent; the ETA may issue enforcement notice with a travel ban and a personal distress action against private movable assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SPV accepting syndicated loan wire funds or convertible debt from undisclosed beneficial owners without a valid Egyptian AML officer, without enhanced due diligence on a PE counterpart, and using parallel Swift payment routes designed to obscure the origin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fine up to EGP 1,000,000 under the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law, suspension of treasury operations, and referral to the Public Prosecutor; the funding channels may be blocked and the SPV placed on the ETA risk blacklist.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for transaction approval may be personally fined and, for knowingly structuring payments to evade disclosure, imprisoned for up to 7 years.
